items.title: Mcbee interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2020
items.q: The transcript only shows Monk Rowe introducing himself as the interviewer; no personal or professional relationship between Cecil McBee and Monk Rowe is described.

ctx.x: He was interviewed on November 6, 2020 via Zoom, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive at Hamilton College, and it’s a privilege today to speak with bassist, composer, and music educator Cecil McBee, who is in Brooklyn and I am in Clinton, New York. And thank you for joining me, Mr. McBee.
Thank you for joining me and having me realized here.

items.title: Mcbee interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2020
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m pleased to have a second session with Cecil McBee

ctx.x: He was interviewed on November 20, 2020 via Zoom, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m pleased to have a second session with Cecil McBee about two weeks after our first conversation. Thanks for finding time again. And you mentioned that you still live, your bio clock, you’re still a nighttime person, is that correct?

Oh yeah. You know when you’re in Tokyo, which is 14 hours in advance of your clock, for a couple of weeks and then you return to New York, supposedly back in reverse to what your rhythm would be about. And then you go to California. And then to Texas. So over all these years I managed to function around this time of the day Eastern Time. I’m up about maybe 11, 11:30.
